chapter_title: We're Not Afraid to Die... if We Can All Be Together

concepts.title: The Dream Voyage and Its Preparation
concepts.definition: The narrator replicates Captain James Cook's round-the-world voyage in his boat Wavewalker, a 23-metre wooden-hulled vessel built for rough seas. He and his wife Mary spend years practising seamanship while working, and set out from Plymouth with crew, testing themselves before the family joins for the final leg.
concepts.key_idea: A dream armed with training -- the voyage begins as preparation long before it becomes ordeal.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb102.txt opening sections ( replicating captain cook voyage, wavewalker boat, honing seafaring skills, route via africa and australia)

solution_steps.explain: The narrator sets out to duplicate Captain Cook's circumnavigation, the voyage of a lifetime.
A sturdy boat, years of practice at sea during off-hours, and a first leg with trained crew show the dream was disciplined, not reckless.
Only the final leg carries wife and children, which sharpens the later crisis into a family trial.

concepts.title: The Storm in the Southern Indian Ocean
concepts.definition: Near the Southern Indian Ocean the family sails into gale-force winds that build over days, and on January 2 a gigantic wave strikes Wavewalker, smashing deck and cabin, throwing the narrator overboard and opening the hull. With the boat half-swamped and the compass gone, the struggle shifts from travel to bare survival.
concepts.key_idea: One mountain of water rewrites the voyage -- from compass course to bucket-and-pump survival.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb102.txt storm section (gales, january 2 wave, capsizing, head smashed, decks broken, pumps, mayday calls)
question_patterns: describe the giant wave that struck wavewalker

solution_steps.explain: A perfect, mighty wave lifts the boat and hurls it; the narrator flies overboard, cracks his head, and is washed back aboard.
Broken timbers, a smashed starboard side, flooded cabins, lost compass and dying engines reduce the boat to a sinking shell.
Canvas and forecastle patches, electric and hand pumps, dinner of tongued salad, and steering with makeshift lashings keep the hull alive.

concepts.title: Courage in the Children: Jon and Sue
concepts.definition: The children's bravery carries the chapter's title. Seven-year-old Jon tells his father he is not afraid to die if the family stays together; twelve-year-old Sue, head swollen from injury, hides her cuts to avoid worry and later draws a heart with a thank-you for the parents' rescue effort. Their composure stiffens the adults.
concepts.key_idea: The smallest sailors teach the largest courage -- not afraid to die, if all are together.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb102.txt children section (jon's words not afraid to die, sue's swollen head, drawing of hearts, if we can all be together)
question_patterns: what did jon say about not being afraid to die

solution_steps.explain: Jon comforts his father by embracing the worst together -- the phrase that names the chapter.
Concealing a deep cut and a swollen head, she spares her parents fear; her heart-drawing later thanks them.
The children's fearless togetherness converts a boat emergency into a family resolve that outlasts the sea.

concepts.title: Landfall at Ile Amsterdam and the Theme of Endurance
concepts.definition: Steering on his estimate of remaining islands, the narrator reaches Ile Amsterdam -- a volcanic speck with a French weather station -- on January 6. Larry and Herbie's help, Mary's level-headed pumping, and the children's cheer complete a portrait of shared endurance: skill, luck and love steering the same tiller.
concepts.key_idea: Calculation plus teamwork plus hope finds land -- survival is a crew sport.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb102.txt closing sections (ile amsterdam, january 6, cheer of the island, theme of collective courage, optimist attitude)

solution_steps.explain: Working from the last fixed position and rough sailing estimates, the narrator aims for the supposed islands.
On January 6 Ile Amsterdam appears; the French weather station marks their rescue and safety.
Between storm and shore lies the chapter's message: united, hopeful, skilled people outlast catastrophe.

worked_examples.question_pattern: List in order the damage-control measures the family took after the giant wave hit Wavewalker.

solution_template.explain: They hammer canvas and tarpaulin over the shattered starboard bow to slow the flooding.
Two electric pumps and a hand pump run continuously to hold the ingress at bay.
With a makeshift tiller and storm jib they steer toward the islands, eating a last supper with prayers.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Justify the title 'We're Not Afraid to Die... if We Can All Be Together' from incidents in the chapter.

solution_template.explain: The boy tells his father that dying is bearable if the family faces it together.
Sue hides her wounds and sends a drawing of hearts, choosing the family's morale over her own pain.
Both acts show fear mastered by togetherness -- the exact promise of the title.
